note: Shortcuts from a situation to the product rows that actually fit it. Every line is written from a field that already exists in the product register - best_for, tradeoff, fit_line, capacity_note or a manufacturer-stated dimension - and every row cites the source that supplied those figures. Nothing here is a popularity claim, a ranking, a computed score or a recommendation of what you should buy. If a product row has no confirmed link yet, the path says so instead of showing a buy button.

paths.situation: You cook two things that need different times
paths.because: Two independent 3 qt baskets in one 6 qt body, with the maker's Sync Finish feature for getting them to the table together.
paths.why_this_row: Two foods, two timers, one footprint. This is the row for a chicken and a tray of potatoes that need to come out together.
paths.tradeoff: Each 3 qt basket is smaller than one 6 qt drawer, so a single large batch gets split.

paths.situation: You are cooking for a group and want it all at once
paths.because: 26 qt of cavity, french doors, and a multi-function convection oven - the largest cavity on this shelf.
paths.why_this_row: Racks, french doors and 26 quarts. This is the row when a basket is the bottleneck, not the oven.
paths.tradeoff: It is a countertop oven, so it needs oven-sized counter depth and it is the largest footprint in this set.

paths.situation: You want one big batch and no divider in the way
paths.because: A single 8 qt basket, so a batch does not have to be split across two drawers.
paths.why_this_row: One basket, eight quarts, nothing to divide. This is the row for a single big batch.
paths.tradeoff: No window and no second basket, so checking food means opening the drawer. The listing and the maker's own page also describe two different 8 qt models - read the conflict note on the product page before ordering.

paths.situation: You want to stop guessing when the meat is done
paths.because: Two ways to do it: a handheld spot check at the grill, or a leave-in wireless probe that reports without you standing next to it.
paths.why_this_row: One reads a spot. One watches the whole cook. Pick by which of those you actually do.
paths.tradeoff: The leave-in probe depends on an app and a hub, so a flat battery or a dropped connection is a cooking problem. The instant-read unit reads one spot at a time.

paths.situation: Your counter space is the real constraint
paths.because: Depth as each manufacturer states it: 10.63 in for the dual-basket fryer, 14.8 in for the french-door oven. Stated capacity: 6 qt against 26 qt.
paths.why_this_row: Two fryers, two very different footprints. The depth figure is the one that decides whether the drawer still opens.
paths.tradeoff: The larger oven buys the rack space and the whole-meat capacity. The smaller fryer keeps the counter usable and leaves the drawer openable. Neither figure is a price, and neither is a recommendation.
